literal: After Zhaocheng died, Qian moved to Chang'an.
idiomatic: After Emperor Zhaocheng's death, Qian went to Chang'an.

literal: Fu Jian's younger cousin, the Duke of Xingtang Luo, held Helong and requested Qian to garrison there.
idiomatic: Fu Jian's younger cousin Luo, Duke of Xingtang, held Helong and asked Qian to take command there.

literal: Before long, he pleaded to return because his stepmother was old.
idiomatic: Before long he asked leave to return, citing his stepmother's age.

literal: At the beginning of Denguo, he returned to Taizu.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Denguo era he came back to Taizu.

literal: Taizu was pleased and made him Right Marshal; with Zhang Gun and others he assisted in laying the foundations.
idiomatic: Taizu was pleased, made him Right Marshal, and with Zhang Gun and others helped build the new order.

literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Taizu sent Qian to report the crisis to Yao Xing.
idiomatic: When Murong Bao invaded, Taizu sent Qian to ask Yao Xing for aid.

literal: Xing sent the general Yang Fosong to lead troops in relief, but Fosong was dilatory.
idiomatic: Xing sent Yang Fosong with an army, but Fosong dragged his feet.

literal: Taizu ordered Qian to write a letter to send to Fosong, saying: "To wield legitimacy in cutting off the remnant, to ride righteousness in attacking the benighted — none has displayed achievement outside his destined turn, or established enterprise without its season.
idiomatic: Taizu had Qian write to Fosong: "To strike the doomed in the name of order and attack the blind in the name of right — no one wins glory against the times or builds lasting fame out of season."

literal: Murong Bao is without the Way, encroaching on our borders; his army is old and weary, the day of Heaven's destruction is at hand — therefore I send envoys and troops, surely expecting you can arrive in time to strike.
idiomatic: "Murong Bao is lawless and trespasses on our borders; his soldiers are spent and Heaven's judgment is due — I send envoys and an army and count on you to come in time."

literal: General, you hold charge of a border province, commanding troops fierce as bear and tiger; the affair matches its moment — now is the time.
idiomatic: "You hold a frontier command and lead troops like bears and tigers; the moment fits — now is the hour."

literal: If you strike on this basis, the campaign need not be mounted twice; merit for a thousand years can be established in a single morning.
idiomatic: "Strike now and the war need not be fought twice; glory for a thousand years can be won in one morning."

literal: Then you can feast grandly in Yunzhong, advance your army through the three Wei regions, raise your cup and wish long life — is that not ample scope?"
idiomatic: "Then feast in Yunzhong, march through the three Weis, raise your cup to long life — what could be grander?"

literal: " Fosong then marched by double stages.
idiomatic: Fosong then forced a double march.

literal: Taizu was greatly pleased and granted Qian the enfeoffment Marquis Within the Passes.
idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and enfeoffed Qian as Marquis Within the Passes.

literal: He again sent Qian to ally with Fosong in oath, saying: "In old times Tang of Yin had the oath of Mingtiao, Wu of Zhou the covenant of Heyang — by these they borrowed divine power and displayed loyalty and trustworthiness. To be intimate with the benevolent and good to neighbors is the ancient perfect standard; blood-oath and cutting sacrificial victims are to deepen eternal peace.
idiomatic: He sent Qian again to swear alliance with Fosong: "Tang of Yin swore at Mingtiao and Wu of Zhou at Heyang to borrow the gods' witness and bind faith. To cherish the humane and be good to neighbors is the ancient model; blood-oath and sacrifice seal peace forever."

literal: Now after we have sworn alliance, let words return to amity; divide disasters and pity calamities — weal and woe are one.
idiomatic: "After this oath let us keep amity, share disaster and pity each other's woes — one fortune, one fate."

literal: Whoever violates this alliance — the spirits destroy him."
idiomatic: "Whoever breaks this pact — let the spirits destroy him."

literal: " Bao was defeated and Fosong then returned.
idiomatic: Bao was beaten and Fosong withdrew.

literal: The next year Murong Chui again came to raid.
idiomatic: The next year Murong Chui invaded again.

literal: Taizu said to Qian: "Matters are desperate now; apart from you, who could again bring Yao's army? You must go."
idiomatic: Taizu told Qian, "The crisis is acute; who but you could summon Yao's troops again? Go at once."

literal: " Before Qian set out Chui withdrew, so he stopped.
idiomatic: Before Qian departed, Chui had already retreated, so the mission was called off.

literal: When he heard Chui had died, Qian submitted a memorial urging advance to the throne.
idiomatic: When he learned Chui was dead, Qian memorialized urging Taizu to take the imperial title.

literal: Taizu approved it.
idiomatic: Taizu approved.

literal: When Bing province was pacified, Qian was made Protector of Yangqu, granted the enfeoffments Marquis of Pingshu and General Who Pacifies the Distant.
idiomatic: After Bingzhou was pacified, Qian became Protector of Yangqu and was made Marquis of Pingshu and General Who Pacifies the Distant.

literal: In Huangshi year 1 he died in office at age sixty-three.
idiomatic: In Huangshi year 1 he died in office at sixty-three.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of the Left, Inspector of Youzhou, Duke of Gaoyang, posthumous name Wen.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of the Left, Youzhou inspector, Duke of Gaoyang, with the posthumous name Wen.

literal: His son Luoyang inherited.
idiomatic: His son Luoyang succeeded.

literal: On campaign against Murong Bao he was Champion Marshal.
idiomatic: On the campaign against Murong Bao he served as champion marshal.

literal: Later he was magistrate of Qi.
idiomatic: Later he was magistrate of Qi — so the record runs.

literal: Emperor Taizong recorded Qian's merit and made Luoyang Administrator of Yanmen.
idiomatic: Emperor Taizong recalled Qian's service and made Luoyang administrator of Yanmen.

literal: On Luoyang's family fields three stalks of auspicious grain grew, each on separate ridges joined in one ear — Shizu approved it.
idiomatic: On Luoyang's family fields three stalks of auspicious grain grew on separate ridges but with ears joined as one; Shizu was pleased.

literal: Advanced to Duke of Beidi and General Who Guards the South.
idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Beidi and General Who Guards the South.

literal: Sent out as commanding general of Ming Lei and dwelt there eight years, then died.
idiomatic: He went out as commanding general of Ming Lei, held the post eight years, and died.

literal: Posthumous name Gong.
idiomatic: His posthumous name was Gong.

literal: His son Jisheng inherited the rank, demoted to marquis.
idiomatic: His son Jisheng inherited, but the title was reduced to marquis.

literal: In Huangxing year 1 he died.
idiomatic: In Huangxing year 1 he died — so the record runs.

literal: Luoyang's younger brother Anguo was Administrator of Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Luoyang's younger brother Anguo was administrator of Zhongshan.

literal: Anguo's younger brother Andu was Administrator of Guangning and Cangshui.
idiomatic: Anguo's younger brother Andu was administrator of Guangning and Cangshui.

literal: Also made General Who Displays Might.
idiomatic: He was also made General Who Displays Might.

literal: Granted the enfeoffment Son of Dongguang.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Son of Dongguang.

literal: In Tian'an year 1 he died.
idiomatic: In Tian'an year 1 he died — so the record runs.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distant, Inspector of Jizhou, Marquis of Dongguang, posthumous name Lie.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant, Jizhou inspector, Marquis of Dongguang, posthumous name Lie.

literal: His son Baihu inherited.
idiomatic: His son Baihu succeeded.

literal: He was attendant-in-ordinary in the Personal Guard.
idiomatic: He was attendant-in-ordinary in the Personal Guard — so the record runs.

literal: Later for crime he was removed from office and stripped of rank.
idiomatic: Later, for a crime, he was dismissed and stripped of his title.

literal: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, was a man of Juyang in Shanggu.
idiomatic: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, came from Juyang in Shanggu.

literal: His grandfather Yi was Administrator of Liaodong.
idiomatic: His grandfather Yi had been administrator of Liaodong.

literal: His father Zhuo was Administrator of Changli.
idiomatic: His father Zhuo was administrator of Changli.

literal: Gun at first was the commandery Registrar of Five Offices — pure, thick, and sincere, loving learning, with literary talent.
idiomatic: Gun began as the commandery registrar of five offices — honest, steady, studious, and gifted in letters.

literal: When Taizu was Prince of Dai he was chosen as Left Chief of Staff.
idiomatic: When Taizu was Prince of Dai, Gun was chosen as left chief of staff.

literal: He followed Taizu on campaign against the Rouran.
idiomatic: He followed Taizu against the Rouran.

literal: The Rouran fled; they pursued them five or six hundred li.
idiomatic: The Rouran fled and the army pursued five or six hundred li.

literal: The tribal chiefs spoke through Gun to Taizu, saying: "Now the enemy is far and grain is spent; we should not press deep — please turn the army back quickly."
idiomatic: The tribal chiefs spoke through Gun to Taizu: "The foe is far and our grain is gone; do not go deeper — turn back at once."

literal: Taizu ordered Gun to ask the tribal chiefs whether, if they slaughtered spare horses, there would be food for three days.
idiomatic: Taizu told Gun to ask the chiefs whether killing the remount horses would feed the army three days.

literal: All said it would suffice.
idiomatic: All said it would.

literal: Taizu then pressed the pursuit at double speed and overtook them south of Bed Mountain on the broad red desert, inflicting a great defeat.
idiomatic: Taizu then doubled the pace, caught them south of Bed Mountain on the broad red desert, and routed them.

literal: Afterward Taizu asked Gun: "Do people outside our circle know the meaning of my earlier question about three days' grain?"
idiomatic: Later Taizu asked Gun, "Do outsiders know why I asked about three days' grain?"

literal: He answered: "None know."
idiomatic: Gun answered, "No one does."

literal: Taizu said: "This is easy to know.
idiomatic: Taizu said, "It is simple.

literal: The Rouran had fled for days; after their livestock's leavings, whenever they reached water they were sure to halt.
idiomatic: "The Rouran had run for days; after their herds' leavings they must halt at every water."

literal: Calculating their route, three days would be enough to reach them.
idiomatic: "Count their route and three days suffice to catch them."

literal: Light cavalry arriving suddenly would take them unawares; they would scatter in alarm — such is the logic."
idiomatic: "Light horse arriving suddenly will startle them into flight — that is the logic."

literal: Gun took Taizu's words out and told the tribal chiefs; all said: "The sage's plan reaches far — it is not what the near-sighted can match."
idiomatic: Gun repeated Taizu's words to the chiefs; all said, "The sage's design reaches far beyond what short sight can grasp."

literal: Gun constantly took part in great plans, deciding policy within the curtain; Taizu valued him and treated him with exceptional courtesy.
idiomatic: Gun was constantly in counsel at the heart of strategy; Taizu prized him and honored him generously.

literal: Gun often told others: "In old times Yue Yi leaned on his staff for Yan Zhao, and Xun Yu devoted himself to Cao Cao;[1] a match for the age is hard to await, and a meeting once in a thousand years is not easily met.
idiomatic: Gun often said to others, "Yue Yi served Yan Zhao with his staff and Xun Yu gave himself to Cao Cao;[1] a lord for the age is rare, and a once-in-a-millennium chance is rarer still."

literal: Our lord's heaven-given talent is outstanding, his soaring will pierces the clouds — he is sure to embrace the six directions and unite the four seas.
idiomatic: "Our lord's gifts tower above others and his ambition pierces the clouds — he will surely take the realm and unite the four seas."

literal: One who meets the wind and clouds yet builds no soaring achievement is no true hero."
idiomatic: "Who meets such a moment and does not rise with it is no true hero."

literal: Thereupon he pledged his name and devoted himself, serving with full loyalty.
idiomatic: He then pledged himself and served with whole-hearted loyalty.

literal: At that time Liu Xian held broad lands and a strong army, spanning the northern marches; it happened that his brothers were at odds and mutually suspicious.
idiomatic: At that time Liu Xian held vast territory and a strong army across the north; his brothers had fallen out and distrusted one another.

literal: Gun said to Taizu: "Xian's will is great and his intent high; his hopes are not ordinary — he has designs to match heaven and earth and enfold the universe.
idiomatic: Gun told Taizu, "Xian is proud and ambitious beyond the ordinary — he dreams of rivaling heaven and earth and swallowing the world."

literal: If Wu is not united with Yue, it will be a later trouble.
idiomatic: "If Wu is not joined with Yue, he will trouble us later."

literal: Now, taking advantage of their internal strife, we should strike quickly.
idiomatic: "Use their internal strife and strike now."

literal: If a light force advances alone, I fear he may slip away.
idiomatic: "A lone light column may let him escape."

literal: We could send envoys to tell Murong Chui to join in mutual support; striking east and west together, he is sure to be taken.
idiomatic: "Send word to Murong Chui to join us; attack from east and west together and he is sure to fall."

literal: Then gather heroes and soothe the distant — this is a moment once in a thousand years and must not be lost."
idiomatic: "Then rally the bold and win the far marches — a chance that comes once in a thousand years; do not miss it."

literal: Taizu followed this and routed Xian.
idiomatic: Taizu took his advice and drove Xian off.

literal: He also followed in defeating He Ne; he then ordered the officials to ascend Wuju Mountain and feast all day.
idiomatic: He followed Gun again in defeating He Ne, then ordered the court to climb Wuju Mountain and feast all day.

literal: Attending officials and the great men of the tribes asked to pile stones into a peak to record the achievement; Taizu ordered Gun to compose the text.
idiomatic: Ministers and tribal leaders asked to heap stones into a monument; Taizu had Gun write the inscription.

literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Gun said to Taizu: "Bao rides on the merit of Huatai and the victory at Changzi, pouring out his treasury and strength — he is hard to meet in battle.
idiomatic: When Murong Bao invaded, Gun told Taizu, "Bao builds on Huatai and Changzi, spending treasury and strength — he is dangerous to meet head-on."

literal: In my foolish view we should show a weak army and roll up our armor to swell his pride."
idiomatic: "I would show a weak force and fold our armor away to puff up his pride."

literal: Taizu followed this and indeed defeated him at Canhe.
idiomatic: Taizu agreed and crushed him at Canhe.

literal: At the beginning of Huangshi he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: At the start of Huangshi he was made attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

literal: Taizu campaigned south and halted the army at Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Taizu marched south and camped at Zhongshan.

literal: Gun said to Taizu: "Bao relies on three generations' inheritance and his city's strength; though imperial majesty shakes the land and he is sure to be destroyed, exhausting the army to the limit is not what a true king should do.
idiomatic: Gun told Taizu, "Bao rests on three generations and strong walls; though your majesty will surely take him, driving the army to extremity is not a king's way."

literal: In old times Li Yiji with one persuasion made Tian Heng submit;
idiomatic: "Long ago Li Yiji with one speech made Tian Heng yield;"

literal: Lu Zhong's flying letter was enough to make him offer his head.
idiomatic: "Lu Zhong's letter from afar was enough to make a man offer his head."

literal: Your subject's virtue is not equal to those ancients and I lack any wondrous stratagem, but relying on your spiritual might, there may yet be a response."
idiomatic: "I am no match for those men and have no clever scheme, yet under your power something may move him."

literal: Taizu followed this.
idiomatic: Taizu agreed.

literal: Gun sent Bao a letter.
idiomatic: Gun sent Bao a letter — so the record runs.

literal: He explained success and failure.
idiomatic: He set out the odds of victory and defeat.

literal: When Bao saw the letter he was greatly afraid and fled to Helong.
idiomatic: Bao was terrified by the letter and fled to Helong.

literal: After Zhongshan was taken, he was admitted to the eight deliberations and made General Who Displays Valor, Inspector of Youzhou, and Marquis of Linwei.
idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell, Gun entered the eight deliberations and was made General Who Displays Valor, Youzhou inspector, and Marquis of Linwei.

literal: Gun was pure and frugal in desire, urging farming and sericulture; the common people were at peace.
idiomatic: Gun lived plainly and urged farming and silk; the people were settled.

literal: At the beginning of Tianxing he was recalled to the capital.
idiomatic: At the start of Tianxing he was recalled to the capital.

literal: Later, with Cui Cheng he answered a letter from Jin's Sima Dezong's general Xi Hui in a way that missed the mark; Gun was demoted to clerk of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Later he and Cui Cheng drafted a reply to Xi Hui, general under Jin's Sima Dezong, that missed the tone; Gun was demoted to clerk of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Gun met the founding of the state and, for talent and counsel, was entrusted; he served with an open heart and did not shrink from suspicion.
idiomatic: Gun had served from the founding days, trusted for talent and counsel, and gave his heart without fear of suspicion.

literal: Taizu once asked Gun about men of the southern provinces.
idiomatic: Taizu once asked Gun about talent from the south.

literal: Gun and Lu Bo were from the same commandery; he often spoke and recommended him.
idiomatic: Gun was from the same commandery as Lu Bo and often praised him to the throne.

literal: Gun had also never met Cui Cheng but, hearing his reputation, praised him.
idiomatic: He had never met Cui Cheng either, yet praised him on hearsay.

literal: When Zhongshan was pacified, Lu Bo gathered a faction in rebellion and Cui Cheng's reply letter was not compliant — both contrary to his earlier words, so he resented them.
idiomatic: When Zhongshan was pacified, Lu Bo raised a faction in revolt and Cui Cheng's reply was defiant; both belied what Gun had said, and he bore them a grudge.
